hook.convey: a fraction drawn on a strip: cut every part smaller, or join parts into bigger ones → the coloured amount stays, only the numbers change → two names for one amount = barabar bhinn (class 5 folded halves; here thirds, quarters, fifths, and joining)

use.hi: Mummy roti ke hisse kabhi chhote kaatti hain, kabhi mila deti hain; roti utni hi rehti hai.
use.en: Mummy sometimes cuts a roti's parts smaller and sometimes joins them; the roti stays the same.

use.hi: Drawing sheet ke hisse chhote karo ya bade, rangeen jagah utni hi rehti hai.
use.en: Make the parts of a drawing sheet smaller or bigger; the coloured space stays the same.

explain.convey: strip in 3 equal parts, 1 coloured = 1/3; each part cut in 2 → 6 parts, 2 coloured = 2/6; the colour did not change → barabar bhinn; the card: a 3/4 strip on its own board, every part cut into 3 in the mind → the child names the new fraction

viewCaption.hi: Yahan dono pattiyan 0 se 1 ki do number line ban gayi hain, ek ke neeche ek; 1/3 aur 2/6 ke nishaan ek hi seedh mein hain.
viewCaption.en: Here the two strips have become two number lines from 0 to 1, one below the other; the marks for 1/3 and 2/6 are in line.

point.hi: Upar 1/3 rangeen hai. Neeche har hissa 2 mein kata, toh 2/6. Rang utna hi hai: yeh barabar bhinn hain.
point.en: 1/3 of the top strip is coloured. Below, every part is cut in 2, so 2/6. The colour is the same: these are equal fractions.

pointAlt.hi: Socho upar wali patti ka har hissa beech se kaat diya. Hisse 6 ho gaye aur rangeen 2, par rang badla nahi: 1/3 aur 2/6 ek hi cheez ke do naam hain.
pointAlt.en: Picture every part of the top strip cut down the middle. There are now 6 parts and 2 coloured, but the colour did not change: 1/3 and 2/6 are two names for one thing.

prompt.hi: Ab socho, is 3/4 wali patti ke har hisse ko 3 barabar hisson mein kaata. Ab kitne mein se kitne hisse rangeen hain?
prompt.en: Now suppose every part of this 3/4 strip is cut into 3 equal parts. Now how many parts out of how many are coloured?

reask.hi: 3/4 wali patti ka har hissa 3 mein kata, toh naya bhinn kaunsa hai?
reask.en: Every part of the 3/4 strip is cut into 3: which is the new fraction?

did.hi: 3/4 ke har hisse ko 3 mein kaat kar naya bhinn nikala
did.en: cut every part of 3/4 into 3 and named the new fraction

viewCaption.hi: Yahan wahi 3/4 wali patti ek gol roti ki tarah bani hai.
viewCaption.en: Here the same 3/4 strip is drawn round like a roti.

why.hi: 4 hisse 3-3 mein kate toh 12, aur 3 rangeen hisse 3 × 3 bane: 9/12
why.en: 4 parts cut in 3 each make 12, and the 3 coloured parts make 3 × 3: 9/12

whyShort.hi: har rangeen hissa bhi 3 mein kata
whyShort.en: every coloured part was cut into 3 too

whyAlt.hi: Kaatne par rangeen hisse bhi kat-te hain: woh utne hi nahi rehte, har ek 3 chhote hisse ban jaata hai.
whyAlt.en: Cutting cuts the coloured parts too: they do not stay as many, each one becomes 3 small parts.

simpler.hi: Pehle socho, 4 hisse 3-3 mein kate toh kul kitne bane. Phir rangeen hisson ke saath bhi wahi socho.
simpler.en: First think how many parts 4 parts make when each is cut into 3. Then think the same for the coloured parts.

hindi.hi: 3/4 wali patti ka har hissa 3 chhote hisson mein baant do. Poori patti mein ab kul kitne bane, aur unmein rang wale kitne?
hindi.en: Split every part of the 3/4 strip into 3 small parts. How many are there now in the whole strip, and how many of them have colour?

simpler.hi: Hisse kaatne se rangeen jagah nahi badalti, sirf hisse chhote aur zyada ho jaate hain. Isliye 1/3 aur 2/6 barabar bhinn hain.
simpler.en: Cutting the parts does not change the coloured space; the parts only get smaller and more. So 1/3 and 2/6 are equal fractions.

explain.convey: the reverse: a strip in 6 parts, 4 coloured; join the parts in twos → 3 bigger parts, 2 coloured → 4/6 = 2/3; the card: 8 of 10 coloured, joined in twos, on its own board → the child names the new fraction

viewCaption.hi: Yahan dono pattiyan 0 se 1 ki do number line ban gayi hain, ek ke neeche ek; 4/6 aur 2/3 ke nishaan ek hi seedh mein hain.
viewCaption.en: Here the two strips have become two number lines from 0 to 1, one below the other; the marks for 4/6 and 2/3 are in line.

point.hi: Ulta bhi hota hai. Upar 6 mein se 4 hisse rangeen hain. Do-do hisse milao, toh 3 bade hisse bante hain aur 2 rangeen: 4/6 = 2/3.
point.en: It works the other way too. On top, 4 of 6 parts are coloured. Join the parts in twos, and 3 big parts form, 2 of them coloured: 4/6 = 2/3.

pointAlt.hi: Ab chhote hisse mila kar bade banao. 6 chhote hisse do-do mile toh 3 bade bane, aur 4 rangeen mile toh 2. Rang wahi raha.
pointAlt.en: Now join small parts into big ones. 6 small parts joined in twos make 3 big ones, and the 4 coloured make 2. The colour stayed the same.

prompt.hi: Ab ek patti ke 10 barabar hisson mein se 8 rangeen hain. Do-do hisse mila kar bade hisse banaye: naya bhinn kya hai?
prompt.en: Now a strip has 8 of its 10 equal parts coloured. The parts are joined in twos into big parts: what is the new fraction?

reask.hi: 8/10 wali patti ke saare hisse do-do milaye, toh kaunsa bhinn bana?
reask.en: All the parts of the 8/10 strip joined in twos: which fraction is it?

did.hi: 10 mein se 8 rangeen hisse do-do mila kar naya bhinn nikala
did.en: joined 8 coloured parts of 10 in twos and named the new fraction

viewCaption.hi: Yahan wahi patti ek gol roti ki tarah bani hai: 10 barabar hisse, aur 8 rangeen.
viewCaption.en: Here the same strip is drawn round like a roti: 10 equal parts, 8 coloured.

why.hi: 10 hisse do-do mil kar 5 bade hisse, aur 8 rangeen mil kar 4: 4/5
why.en: 10 parts joined in twos make 5 big parts, and the 8 coloured make 4: 4/5

whyShort.hi: rangeen aur kul, dono do-do mile
whyShort.en: the coloured and all parts joined in twos

whyAlt.hi: Milane par poori patti ke hisse bhi milte hain; neeche 10 nahi rehta, kyunki bade hisse 10 nahi bante.
whyAlt.en: Joining joins the parts of the whole strip too; the bottom does not stay 10, because there are not 10 big parts.

simpler.hi: Pehle gino, 10 hisse do-do mil kar kitne bade hisse bante hain. Phir rangeen hisse bhi do-do milao.
simpler.en: First count how many big parts 10 parts make when joined in twos. Then join the coloured parts in twos too.

simpler.hi: Do-do hisse milane se hisse bade aur kam ho jaate hain, par rang utna hi rehta hai. Isliye 4/6 aur 2/3 barabar hain.
simpler.en: Joining parts in twos makes the parts bigger and fewer, but the colour stays the same. So 4/6 and 2/3 are equal.

explain.convey: bigger numbers are not a bigger amount: 1/4 cut in 3 → 3/12, bigger numbers, the same colour; the card: Reena 3/5 of a roti, Mohit 9/15 of the same roti → who ate more, or the same

viewCaption.hi: Yahan dono pattiyan 0 se 1 ki do number line ban gayi hain, ek ke neeche ek; 1/4 aur 3/12 ke nishaan ek hi seedh mein hain.
viewCaption.en: Here the two strips have become two number lines from 0 to 1, one below the other; the marks for 1/4 and 3/12 are in line.

point.hi: Sirf numbers dekh kar nahi keh sakte ki bhinn bada hai. 1/4 ke har hisse ko 3 mein kaato, toh 3/12 banta hai: numbers bade hain, par rang utna hi.
point.en: From the numbers alone you cannot say a fraction is bigger. Cut every part of 1/4 into 3 and you get 3/12: the numbers are bigger, but the colour is the same.

pointAlt.hi: 3/12 mein 3 aur 12 bade dikhte hain, par uske hisse 1/4 ke hisson se chhote hain. Isliye zyada hisse milkar bhi utna hi rang banta hai.
pointAlt.en: In 3/12 the 3 and 12 look bigger, but its parts are smaller than the parts of 1/4. So more parts together still make the same colour.

prompt.hi: Reena ne ek roti ka 2/3 khaaya, Mohit ne waisi hi roti ka 8/12. Kisne zyada khaaya, ya dono ne barabar?
prompt.en: Reena ate 2/3 of a roti, Mohit 8/12 of a roti just like it. Who ate more, or did both eat the same?

reask.hi: 2/3 roti aur waisi roti ka 8/12: kaun zyada hai, ya dono barabar?
reask.en: 2/3 of a roti and 8/12 of the same kind of roti: which is more, or are they the same?

did.hi: 2/3 aur 8/12 roti ki tulna karke dekha ki dono barabar hain
did.en: compared 2/3 and 8/12 of a roti and saw they are the same

viewCaption.en: Here both rotis are drawn round: the first in three equal parts, the second in twelve, none coloured yet.

why.hi: Mohit ke hisse chaar-chaar milao: 12 se 3 bade hisse, 8 se 2. 8/12 = 2/3, toh dono ne barabar khaaya
why.en: Join Mohit's parts in fours: 12 make 3 big parts, 8 make 2. 8/12 = 2/3, so both ate the same

whyAlt.hi: Mohit isliye laga ki 8, 2 se bada hai; par Mohit ki roti ke hisse chhote hain, isliye sirf ginti se roti ka pata nahi chalta.
whyAlt.en: It looked like Mohit because 8 is bigger than 2; but Mohit's roti has small parts, so the count alone does not tell the amount of roti.

simpler.hi: Mohit ki roti ke hisse chaar-chaar mila kar bade hisse banao. Phir uske khaaye hisse Reena ke hisson se tulna karo.
simpler.en: Join the parts of Mohit's roti in fours into big parts. Then match the parts he ate against Reena's.

hindi.hi: Do ek jaisi roti hain. Reena ke paas ek ka 2/3 hai aur Mohit ke paas doosri ka 8/12: kiske paas roti zyada hai, ya dono ke paas barabar?
hindi.en: There are two identical rotis. Reena has 2/3 of one and Mohit 8/12 of the other: who has more roti, or do both have the same?

simpler.hi: Hisse chhote hon toh ginti badh jaati hai, par rang wahi rehta hai. Numbers dekh kar bhinn bada mat samjho.
simpler.en: When the parts are smaller the count grows, but the colour stays the same. Do not take a fraction as bigger from its numbers.

problem.hi: Do ek jaisi pattiyan: pehli ke 8 barabar hisson mein se 6 rangeen, doosri ke 12 mein se 9. Hisse mila kar dekhenge, rang utna hi hai ya nahi.
problem.en: Two identical strips: 6 of the first one's 8 parts are coloured, 9 of the second one's 12. We will join parts and check if the colour is the same.

problemAlt.hi: Socho do ek jaisi chocolate hain: ek ke 8 hisson mein se 6 kha liye, doosri ke 12 mein se 9. Hisse mila kar dekhenge ki dono se barabar khaaya ya nahi.
problemAlt.en: Picture two identical chocolates: 6 of one's 8 parts are eaten, 9 of the other's 12. We will join parts and see whether the same was eaten from both.

simpler.hi: Dono pattiyon ke hisse alag size ke hain, isliye sirf ginti ki tulna kaafi nahi. Pehle dono ke hisse ek size ke banane honge.
simpler.en: The two strips have parts of different sizes, so comparing the counts is not enough. First the parts of both must be made one size.

givens.hi: pehli patti: 8 barabar hisse, 6 rangeen; doosri: 12 barabar hisse, 9 rangeen; dono ek jaisi
givens.en: first strip: 8 equal parts, 6 coloured; second: 12 equal parts, 9 coloured; both identical

find.en: whether the two strips have the same colour

prompt.en: Into how many big parts will you join both, coloured ones joining whole?

reask.en: Into how many big parts can both 8 parts and 12 parts join equally, with the coloured parts joining whole too?

right.hi: Sahi, 4: dono pattiyan 4 barabar bade hisson mein mil jaati hain.
right.en: Right, 4: both strips join equally into 4 big parts.

hindi.hi: Kitne bade hisse banaoge, jinmein dono pattiyon ke chhote hisse barabar-barabar jaayein, rangeen bhi?
hindi.en: How many big parts will you make, into which the small parts of both strips go equally, the coloured ones too?

whyAlt.hi: Milane se hisse kam hote hain, zyada nahi. Bade hisse utne chuno ki 8 bhi aur 12 bhi unmein barabar bant jaayein, aur rangeen hisse bhi.
whyAlt.en: Joining makes fewer parts, not more. Choose as many big parts as both 8 and 12 split into equally, and the coloured parts too.

pictureCaption.hi: Yahan pehli patti hai, 8 barabar hisson mein, aur 6 rangeen.
pictureCaption.en: Here is the first strip, in 8 equal parts, 6 coloured.

do.hi: Dono pattiyon ko 4 bade hisson mein lao
do.en: Bring both strips to 4 big parts

why.hi: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 aur 12 ÷ 4 = 3; rangeen 6 aur 9 bhi poore milte hain
why.en: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3; the coloured 6 and 9 join whole too

simpler.hi: Socho, kitne bade hisse banein ki 8 bhi aur 12 bhi unmein barabar baant sakein. Phir socho, rangeen hisse bhi poore baithte hain ya nahi.
simpler.en: Think how many big parts would let both 8 and 12 be shared equally into them. Then think whether the coloured parts fit whole too.

told.hi: Dono ko 4 bade hisson mein laayenge: dono pattiyan 4 barabar hisson mein mil jaati hain.
told.en: We bring both to 4 big parts: both strips join equally into 4.

do.hi: Pehli patti ke do-do hisse milao
do.en: Join the first strip's parts in twos

steps.result: pehli patti ke 6 rangeen do-do mil kar 3

why.en: 8 ÷ 4 = 2, so the parts join in twos

simpler.hi: Pehli patti ke chhote hisse barabar baant kar bade hisse banao, aur rangeen hisse bhi usi tarah milao.

told.hi: Pehli patti ke do-do hisse milaye: 4 bade hisse bane, aur 6 rangeen mil kar 3.
told.en: We joined the first strip's parts in twos: 4 big parts formed, and the 6 coloured became 3.

prompt.en: Your turn: join the second strip's 12 parts into 4 big parts too. Now how many of the 4 big parts are coloured?

reask.hi: Doosri patti 4 bade hisson mein: unmein se rangeen kitne bane?
reask.en: The second strip in 4 big parts: how many of them are coloured?

did.hi: doosri patti ke hisse mila kar 9/12 ko 4 bade hisson mein likha
did.en: joined the second strip's parts and wrote 9/12 in 4 big parts

why.hi: 4 toh kul bade hisse hain; sawaal yeh hai ki unmein se kitnon mein rang hai.
why.en: 4 is all the big parts; the question is how many of them have colour.

viewCaption.hi: Yahan wahi patti ek gol roti ki tarah bani hai: 12 barabar hisse, aur 9 rangeen.
viewCaption.en: Here the same strip is drawn round like a roti: 12 equal parts, 9 coloured.

why.hi: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, toh teen-teen milte hain; 9 rangeen teen-teen mil kar 3 bade bane
why.en: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so they join in threes; the 9 coloured join into 3 big ones

whyAlt.hi: 9 toh chhote rangeen hisson ki ginti hai; bade hisse banane par rangeen chhote hisse bhi group mein milte hain, woh 9 nahi rehte.
whyAlt.en: 9 is the count of small coloured parts; when big parts are made the small coloured parts join in groups too, and they do not stay 9.

simpler.hi: Pehle socho, ek bade hisse mein doosri patti ke kitne chhote hisse jaate hain. Phir rangeen chhote hisson ko bhi utne-utne milao.
simpler.en: First think how many of the second strip's small parts go into one big part. Then join the coloured small parts in the same groups.

answer.hi: Dono mein rang utna hi hai: dono mein 4 mein se 3 bade hisse rangeen. 6/8 aur 9/12 dono 3/4 hain.
answer.en: Both have the same colour: in both, 3 of 4 big parts are coloured. 6/8 and 9/12 are both 3/4.

why.hi: dono pattiyon ke hisse mila kar ek size ke kiye, aur dono mein 4 mein se 3 bade hisse rangeen nikle
why.en: we made both strips' parts one size by joining, and both came out with 3 of 4 big parts coloured

reask.hi: 12 hisson wale cake ke kitne hisse 6 mein se 5 ke barabar honge?
reask.en: How many parts of the 12-part cake equal 5 of 6?

did.hi: 6 mein se 5 ke barabar 12 mein se hisse nikale
did.en: found the parts out of 12 that equal 5 out of 6

viewCaption.hi: Yahan pehla cake ek seedhi patti ki tarah khula hai: 6 barabar hisse, aur 5 rangeen.

why.hi: 12 hisse karne ke liye har hissa 2 mein kata, toh 5 hisse 5 × 2 = 10 chhote hisson ke barabar
why.en: To make 12 parts every part is cut in 2, so 5 parts equal 5 × 2 = 10 small parts

whyShort.hi: har bada hissa 2 chhote hisson jitna
whyShort.en: every big part is as much as 2 small parts

whyAlt.hi: Doosre cake ke hisse chhote hain; utne hi hisse lene se cake kam aata hai, isliye ginti badhni chahiye.

say.hi: Ek baar bhaag dene ke baad bhi upar aur neeche mein koi common factor bacha ho sakta hai. Jab tak ek se bada common factor bache, aur bhaag do.
say.en: Even after dividing once, the top and bottom may still share a common factor. While a common factor bigger than one is left, divide again.

simpler.hi: Har bhaag ke baad dono numbers ke factor dekho; jab tak koi aur common factor dikhe, bhaag karte raho.
simpler.en: After each division look at the factors of both numbers; while another common factor turns up, keep dividing.

sayAlt.hi: Ek bhaag ke baad ruk jaana seedhi ke beech mein ruk jaane jaisa hai. Upar tab pahunchoge jab common factor sirf 1 bache.
sayAlt.en: Stopping after one division is like stopping halfway up a ladder. You reach the top when the only common factor left is 1.

prompt.hi: 48/66 ko 2 se bhaag diya toh 24/33 aaya. Ise lowest terms tak le jao.
prompt.en: 48/66 divided by 2 gave 24/33. Take it to lowest terms.

reask.hi: 24/33 lowest terms mein kya hai?
reask.en: What is 24/33 in lowest terms?

viewCaption.hi: Board par baayein upar ka 48 ÷ 2 = 24 hai, aur daayein neeche ka 66 ÷ 2 = 33.

why.hi: 24 aur 33 dono 3 se bat-te hain: 24 ÷ 3 = 8, 33 ÷ 3 = 11, toh 8/11
why.en: 24 and 33 both divide by 3: 24 ÷ 3 = 8, 33 ÷ 3 = 11, so 8/11

whyShort.hi: 8/11 se aage koi bhaag nahi bachta

whyAlt.hi: 24/33 ko aur chhota kar sakte ho: 3 se 24 bhi bat-ta hai aur 33 bhi.

simpler.hi: 24/33 ke upar aur neeche ka common factor dhoondo aur bhaag do. Phir jaancho, kuch common bacha toh nahi.
simpler.en: Find a common factor of the top and bottom of 24/33 and divide. Then check whether anything common is left.

say.hi: Hisse chhote kaato toh numbers bade ho jaate hain, par rang utna hi rehta hai. Isliye numbers nahi, rang ki tulna karo: dono ko lowest terms ya ek size ke hisson mein lao.
say.en: Cut the parts smaller and the numbers get bigger, but the colour stays the same. So compare the colour, not the numbers: bring both to lowest terms or to parts of one size.

simpler.hi: Numbers dekh kar faisla mat karo. Dono bhinn ko lowest terms mein lao, phir tulna karo.
simpler.en: Do not decide by the numbers. Bring both fractions to lowest terms, then compare.

sayAlt.hi: Ek hi roti ko 4 hisson mein kaato ya 12 mein, roti wahi rehti hai. 12 hisson mein se 9 aur 4 mein se 3, dono utni hi roti hai.
sayAlt.en: Cut one roti into 4 parts or into 12, it is the same roti. 9 of 12 parts and 3 of 4 are the same amount of roti.

why.hi: 6/8 ka lowest terms 3/4 hai, aur 15/20 ka bhi 3/4: dono barabar

whyAlt.hi: 15/20 ko uske bade numbers dekh kar chuna; par uske hisse 6/8 ke hisson se chhote hain, toh sirf numbers se bada nahi keh sakte.
whyAlt.en: 15/20 was picked for its bigger numbers; but its parts are smaller than those of 6/8, so the numbers alone cannot say it is bigger.

simpler.hi: 6/8 aur 15/20, dono ko lowest terms mein likho, aur dekho kya bana.

covered.hi: Aakhir mein bhinn ko common factor se bhaag dete gaye, jab tak sirf 1 common bacha: lowest terms.

prompt.hi: Ek dabbe ke 27 laddoo mein se 21 meethe hain, doosre ke 36 mein se 28. Pehle dabbe ke meethe laddoo ka bhinn lowest terms mein kya hai, aur doosre ka?
prompt.en: In one box 21 of 27 laddoos are sweet, in another 28 of 36. What is the fraction of sweet laddoos in the first box in lowest terms, and in the second?

reask.hi: 21/27 aur 28/36, dono lowest terms mein kya hain?
reask.en: What are 21/27 and 28/36 in lowest terms?

did.hi: do dabbon ke meethe laddoo ke bhinn lowest terms mein likhe

why.hi: 21/27 ko 3 se bhaag do toh 7/9, aur 28/36 ko 4 se toh 7/9. Dono dabbon mein bhinn ek hi hai.
why.en: Divide 21/27 by 3 and you get 7/9, and 28/36 by 4 gives 7/9. The fraction is the same in both boxes.

simpler.hi: Pehle 21/27 ke upar aur neeche ka common factor dhoondo aur bhaag do. Phir 28/36 ke saath bhi yahi karo.
simpler.en: First find a common factor of the top and bottom of 21/27 and divide. Then do the same with 28/36.

whyAlt.hi: Ek baar bhaag ke baad bhi jaancho ki upar aur neeche mein koi common factor bacha hai ya nahi; har dabbe ka bhinn alag se lowest terms tak lao.
whyAlt.en: Even after dividing once, check whether the top and bottom still share a common factor; take each box's fraction to lowest terms on its own.
